correctness.rationale: For any cross-part swap, the internal pairwise sums change by D_A(y)-D_A(x)-d(x,y) and D_B(x)-D_B(y)-d(x,y), exactly matching the aggregate reduction in the two participants’ own average neighbor-distance costs after a,b normalization. Strict improvement implies strict increase and finite assignments ensure termination. The K_{2,5} seven-agent table enumerates all 21 labeled small-side placements via seven type multisets and every cross swap; independent exact-rational code checks all 21 and 212,500 additional identities. Boundary cases a=1 or b=1 and repeated types are included. The proof does not rely on finite tests to infer all-size truth.

value.rationale: Irregular bicliques are an especially natural social network topology excluded by the initiating paper’s regular-graph FIP argument. The exact within-part bilateral potential guarantees convergence for every possible type multiset and every improvement sequence, a structural rather than numerical result; the K_{2,5} exact PoS 17/15 witness proves this stable family can have an inefficient social best equilibrium, delimiting the known regular/path PoS=1 phenomenon.
